resources.string: To record app usage and give you a pause reminder when your vow limit is reached, finish the basic setup first. Notifications, battery, and auto-start are optional reliability boosts.
Why enable this: Tiny Vow needs this system setting to record daily usage for each app.\n\nCurrent status: the basic setup is ready, and usage can be recorded normally.
Why enable this: Tiny Vow needs this system setting to know how long the target app was used today.\n\nHow to enable: tap the button below -> find Tiny Vow in the system list -> enable usage access.
After tapping the button above, open the system Usage Access page, find Tiny Vow, and allow access. The home page refreshes automatically when you return.
This stage does not add system-level hard stops or sync. It focuses on permission checks, target app selection, today usage reading, daily vow storage, and limit reminders.

Why enable this: when a target app reaches its vow limit and is in the foreground, Tiny Vow shows a full-screen reminder to help you pause.\n\nCurrent status: the service is running and vow reminders are active.

Why enable this: when a target app reaches its vow limit in the foreground, this service can show a full-screen reminder to help you bring your attention back.\n\nHow to enable: tap the button below -> find Tiny Vow Reminder Service in the system accessibility service list -> enable the service.

Purpose: some phone vendors tighten background work, which may affect reminder and reminder reliability.\n\nNote: this is optional. Core features still work without it. After tapping the button, look for Auto-start or Allow background activity in system app details.
If reminders or popups stop appearing, check each system setting to make sure permissions were not revoked.
Current status: battery optimization exemption is granted, so background reminders and statistics should be more stable.

Purpose: reduce reminder delays caused by screen-off or battery saving policies.\n\nNote: this is optional. Core features still work without it. After tapping the button, the system decides whether Tiny Vow can be added to the battery allowlist.
Why enable this: when your vow limit is reached, Tiny Vow can also post a local notification.\n\nCurrent status: enabled. Local notifications can be received.

Why enable this: besides the full-screen reminder, this permission lets Tiny Vow show your daily vow status in the notification shade.\n\nHow to enable: tap the button below -> grant notification permission.

Some phone vendors tighten background work. Background start is an optional reliability setting that reduces the chance that timers, reminders, or vow services are cleared by the system. You can skip it and keep the core features.

The battery allowlist is an optional reliability setting. It reduces the chance that reminders and background stats are delayed after system sleep. Tiny Vow still works if you deny or skip it, but some reminders may be less timely.

Tiny Vow reads local app usage data, including package names, app names, foreground usage time, launch counts, sessions, and night usage statistics. This powers daily vows, reports, points, and reminders. By default, the data stays on this device and is not uploaded automatically.

Tiny Vow\'s accessibility service only listens for window changes. It checks whether you entered an app with a configured vow and shows Tiny Vow\'s reminder page when the vow limit is reached. It does not read screen text, click on your behalf, or change system settings.

Tiny Vow uses notification permission to send local vow reminders and vow limit alerts, so you can see today\'s plan in time. Denying notifications does not affect core features such as vows, stats, or vow reminders.
